query: What visit-note signals suggest a longer visit?

per_column.name: visit_type
per_column.rationale: Categorises encounter type (acute/chronic/preventive), a genuine axis plausibly correlated with visit length. Values match source text well across samples.

per_column.name: active_problem_count
per_column.rationale: Problem burden is a reasonable predictor of duration. However groundedness is shaky: the URI note lists essentially one problem (count 1 ok), but the annual physical mapped to 2 despite only fatigue as a symptom, and the acne visit (single condition) shows 2. The count often appears inflated/loosely derived.

per_column.name: clinical_severity
per_column.rationale: Acuity is a strong candidate signal for visit length. Sample categorisations (low/moderate) are well warranted by the text.

per_column.name: critical_stabilizing_action
per_column.rationale: Emergent stabilisation would lengthen visits, so useful. But the acne row labelled 'acute_treatment_in_visit' is a stretch—starting a topical/oral med is routine prescribing, not an in-visit stabilising action; overreads the source.

per_column.name: imaging_or_diagnostic_ordered
per_column.rationale: Ordering imaging plausibly extends visits. Echo and MRI rows are correct, but the annual physical labelled 'point_of_care_only' has no POC imaging mentioned—only labs; an invented diagnostic.

per_column.name: laboratory_test_ordered
per_column.rationale: A single boolean but a meaningful workup signal for duration. Physical/MI rows (labs ordered) correct; however the knee-injury row marked True has no labs in the text, only MRI—unsupported.

per_column.name: specialist_consult_urgency
per_column.rationale: Consult/referral urgency is a plausible length driver. Knee row inferring 'routine_outpatient_referral' is a soft inference from MRI-to-rule-out-tear, not explicitly stated. Largely redundant with specialist_consult_or_referral.

per_column.name: medication_change_type
per_column.rationale: Med changes require counseling time, relevant to duration. Acne row 'new_medication_started' correct; MI/physical 'not_present' correct.

per_column.name: counseling_topic_type
per_column.rationale: Counseling content relates to visit length. Categorisations are reasonable readings, though some are inferred (physical→lifestyle) where the note is terse.

per_column.name: shared_decision_making_documented
per_column.rationale: Mostly false (186/250) and near-constant; weak signal. Sample values conservatively False where text is silent, which is acceptable.

per_column.name: specialist_consult_or_referral
per_column.rationale: Strongly redundant with specialist_consult_urgency (same category vocabulary, near-identical distribution), adding little new leverage. Knee referral is an inference not explicit in text.

judge.rationale: Most added columns give genuine, distinct axes (visit_type, severity, workup ordered, med change, counseling) directly relevant to what drives visit length, so table-level usefulness is solid. Two consult columns are largely redundant with each other and shared_decision_making is near-constant, dragging usefulness down slightly. Groundedness is generally sound—categorical readings track the notes and silent rows default reasonably—but several rows show overreach: invented labs/imaging on the physical and knee rows, an inflated active_problem_count, and a debatable 'acute_treatment' label for routine prescribing. These recurring confident specifics beyond the text keep groundedness at moderate-high rather than high.
